title: Grade 3 Science — Fri, May 22
description: Light and Sound — Basics — Last Week Day 5
subject: science

questions.question: What is the main source of light on Earth?
questions.explanation: The sun is Earth's main natural source of light and energy. Without sunlight, life on Earth would not exist.

questions.question: Light travels in:
questions.explanation: Light travels in straight lines — this is why shadows are formed and why you can't see around corners.

questions.question: A shadow is formed when:
questions.explanation: A shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light, preventing it from reaching the area behind the object.

questions.question: Transparent objects:
options: Let some light through but you can't see clearly through them
Let all light through so you can see clearly through them
questions.explanation: Transparent objects (like glass) allow light to pass through clearly — you can see through them.

questions.question: What happens when light hits a mirror?
questions.explanation: Mirrors have a smooth, shiny surface that reflects light — this is why we can see our reflection in a mirror.

questions.question: Sound is produced by:
questions.explanation: Sound is produced when objects vibrate. These vibrations travel through air (or other materials) to reach our ears.

questions.question: Can sound travel in outer space (vacuum)?
options: No, sound needs a medium (matter) to travel through
questions.explanation: Sound cannot travel in a vacuum (empty space). It needs matter — like air, water, or solid — to travel through.

questions.question: What is an echo?
questions.explanation: An echo is when sound bounces off a hard surface and returns to the listener. You hear echoes in caves and valleys.

questions.question: Which travels faster — light or sound?
options: They travel at the same speed
questions.explanation: Light travels much faster than sound — light reaches us almost instantly; sound travels about 340 m/s. That's why we see lightning before hearing thunder.

questions.question: Materials that do NOT let light pass through are called:
questions.explanation: Opaque materials block all light — like wood, metal, and stone. They form clear, sharp shadows.

questions.question: When a guitar string is plucked, it makes sound by:
questions.explanation: Plucking a guitar string makes it vibrate — these vibrations travel through air as sound waves to our ears.

questions.question: Why do we see the colours of a rainbow?
options: White light from the sun splits into 7 colours when passing through raindrops
questions.explanation: White light is made of 7 colours. When it passes through water droplets (like a prism), it splits into red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet (ROYGBIV).

questions.question: A louder sound has:
questions.explanation: Loudness (volume) depends on amplitude — larger vibrations = louder sound. Measured in decibels (dB).

questions.question: Which of these is a source of ARTIFICIAL light?
questions.explanation: A light bulb is artificial (man-made) light. The sun, moon (reflected), and lightning are natural sources.

questions.question: How do we protect our ears from loud noise?
questions.explanation: Very loud sounds can damage hearing. Ear defenders (ear muffs) or earplugs protect the ears from loud noise.
